q: In what year did Brazil win its fifth men’s World Cup?
hint: For scale: Brazil won its first World Cup, in Sweden, in 1958.
clue: Spain won its first World Cup in 2010.
card: Ronaldo scored both goals in the final against Germany in Yokohama, four years after falling ill on the day of the 1998 final.

q: How many minutes of playing time does a rugby union match have?
hint: For scale: an ice hockey game has three 20-minute periods.
clue: A soccer match has 90 minutes of play.
card: The clock keeps running past full time until the ball goes dead, so the last play can last for minutes.

q: What height did Cuba’s Javier Sotomayor clear in 1993 to set the men’s high jump world record?
hint: For scale: an average adult man is about {1.75 m} tall.
clue: A basketball rim hangs {3.05 m} above the floor.
card: He set it in Salamanca, Spain, clearing a bar about half a meter above his own head.

q: How many points is a try worth in rugby union?
hint: For scale: the conversion kick after a try adds 2 points.
clue: A penalty kick between the posts earns 3 points.
card: Tries were once worth nothing at all: scoring one only gave a team the chance to “try” a kick at goal.

q: In what year did India win its first men’s Cricket World Cup?
hint: For scale: India became independent in 1947.
clue: Sachin Tendulkar made his Test debut for India in 1989.
card: Kapil Dev’s side beat the West Indies, two-time defending champions, in the final at Lord’s in London.

q: How many players does each team have on the field in Australian rules football?
hint: For scale: a soccer team fields 11 players.
clue: A rugby league team fields 13 players.
card: It’s played on an oval cricket ground, often more than {150 m} long.

q: How far did Bob Beamon leap at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics, setting a long jump world record?
hint: For scale: a typical family car is about {4.5 m} long.
clue: A full-size soccer goal is {7.32 m} wide.
card: He beat the old world record by more than half a meter, and his mark stood for almost 23 years.

q: How many Oscars did Slumdog Millionaire (2008), set in Mumbai, win?
hint: For scale: no film has ever won more than 11 Oscars.
clue: The Last Emperor (1987), filmed in Beijing’s Forbidden City, won 9 Oscars.
card: A. R. Rahman won two of them, for the score and for the song “Jai Ho.”

q: In what year was Studio Ghibli’s Princess Mononoke released in Japan?
hint: For scale: Ghibli’s My Neighbor Totoro came out in 1988.
clue: Ghibli’s Porco Rosso, about a pilot cursed to look like a pig, came out in 1992.
card: For a short while it was Japan’s highest-grossing film ever, until Titanic overtook it.

q: How tall was Godzilla in the original 1954 Japanese film?
hint: For scale: a 10-story building is about {30 m} tall.
clue: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is about {56 m} tall.
card: Later films kept making him bigger as Tokyo’s skyline grew, so he could still tower over the city.

q: How long is Christopher Nolan’s Interstellar (2014), in minutes?
hint: For scale: Gravity (2013), another space film, runs 91 minutes.
clue: Ridley Scott’s Gladiator (2000) runs 155 minutes.
card: Its black hole was rendered from physicist Kip Thorne’s equations, and the work led to real scientific papers.

q: How many episodes of the anime Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood were made?
hint: For scale: most anime seasons run 12 or 13 episodes.
clue: Cowboy Bebop ran for 26 episodes.
card: It follows Hiromu Arakawa’s manga to its ending, which the first anime series from 2003 didn’t have yet.

q: How many episodes are in the Korean drama Crash Landing on You?
hint: For scale: a typical US network drama season runs about 22 episodes.
clue: The British drama Sherlock made 13 episodes in total.
card: A South Korean heiress paraglides into North Korea by accident; its two leads later married in real life.

q: In what year was Bruce Lee’s Enter the Dragon released?
hint: For scale: Bruce Lee was born in San Francisco in 1940.
clue: The first Planet of the Apes film came out in 1968.
card: Bruce Lee died six days before it premiered in Hong Kong, so he never saw it become a worldwide hit.

q: In what year did Queen release “Bohemian Rhapsody”?
hint: For scale: Freddie Mercury was born in Zanzibar in 1946.
clue: Queen formed in London in 1970.
card: It has no chorus, and the band’s label was sure it was far too long for radio play.

q: In what year did Daddy Yankee release “Gasolina”?
hint: For scale: “Despacito,” which he also sang on, came out in 2017.
clue: The “Macarena” became a worldwide dance craze in 1996.
card: In 2023 it became the first reggaeton song chosen for the US Library of Congress’s National Recording Registry.

q: In what year did the Spice Girls release their first single, “Wannabe”?
hint: For scale: Madonna’s “Like a Virgin” came out in 1984.
clue: Michael Jackson’s album Dangerous came out in 1991.
card: It topped the charts in more than 30 countries and is the best-selling single ever by a girl group.

q: How many movements are in Vivaldi’s The Four Seasons, all four concertos together?
hint: For scale: it is four violin concertos, one for each season.
clue: Holst’s suite The Planets has seven movements, one per planet.
card: Vivaldi printed sonnets with them, probably his own, describing the birdsong, storms and barking dog in the music.

q: How long is a Steinway Model D concert grand piano?
hint: For scale: an upright piano is about {1.5 m} wide.
clue: A concert harp stands about {1.8 m} tall.
card: It is the piano found on most of the world’s big concert stages.

q: How long is John Lennon’s “Imagine,” in seconds?
hint: For scale: the Beatles’ “Hey Jude” runs over seven minutes.
clue: Queen’s “We Will Rock You” runs about two minutes.
card: Lennon said Yoko Ono deserved a co-writing credit for its ideas, and in 2017 she finally received one.

q: How many strings does a standard Russian balalaika have?
hint: For scale: a guitar has six strings.
clue: A violin has four strings.
card: It’s known for its triangular body; the biggest, the contrabass balalaika, rests on the floor like a cello.

q: In what year did Japan’s Sanrio create Hello Kitty?
hint: For scale: Mickey Mouse first appeared in 1928.
clue: Nintendo’s Donkey Kong arcade game, Mario’s debut, came out in 1981.
card: According to Sanrio, she isn’t really a cat but a cheerful little girl who lives just outside London.

q: How many squares are on a shogi (Japanese chess) board?
hint: For scale: a chessboard is 8 squares by 8.
clue: An international draughts board has 100 squares.
card: Captured pieces can be dropped back onto the board on your side, so games rarely run out of pieces.

q: In what year did the first Angry Birds game come out?
hint: For scale: Tetris was created in Moscow in 1984.
clue: Pokémon Go sent players outdoors in 2016.
card: Its maker, Rovio of Finland, had released 51 games before it.

q: How many tiles come in a standard Rummikub set, jokers included?
hint: For scale: a deck of playing cards has 52 cards.
clue: A full mahjong set usually has 144 tiles.
card: It was invented in the 1940s by Ephraim Hertzano, and Turkey’s hugely popular okey uses the same number of tiles.

q: How many triangular points are on a backgammon board?
hint: For scale: the board is split into four quarters, with the bar down the middle.
clue: A dartboard is split into 20 numbered sections.
card: Its ancestors go back about 5,000 years, to boards found at the Burnt City in Iran.

q: In Minecraft, how many blocks wide is one chunk of the world?
hint: For scale: a Minecraft player stands just under two blocks tall.
clue: A classic Tetris playfield is 10 squares wide.
card: The game loads and saves the world a chunk at a time, which is how its worlds can be practically endless.

q: How many pieces are in LEGO’s 2017 Ultimate Collector Series Millennium Falcon?
hint: For scale: a small LEGO car set usually has a few hundred pieces.
clue: LEGO’s Titanic set has 9,090 pieces.
card: The finished model is more than {80 cm} long.

q: How tall is Lotte World Tower in Seoul?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower is about {330 m} tall.
clue: Shanghai’s Jin Mao Tower is {421 m} tall.
card: Its observation deck has a glass floor, so visitors can look straight down at Seoul from the 118th floor.

q: How tall are the twin spires of Cologne Cathedral in Germany?
hint: For scale: the dome of London’s St Paul’s Cathedral rises about {111 m}.
clue: Salisbury Cathedral’s spire in England is {123 m} tall.
card: Building began in 1248 and wasn’t finished for more than 600 years.

q: How long is the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge, its undersea tunnel included?
hint: For scale: the Øresund link between Denmark and Sweden runs about {16 km}.
clue: The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway in the US is about {38 km} long.
card: Its tunnel runs between two artificial islands, so big ships can still pass over it.

q: In what year did construction of Barcelona’s Sagrada Família begin?
hint: For scale: its architect, Antoni Gaudí, was born in 1852.
clue: The Eiffel Tower was finished in 1889.
card: Gaudí took over a year after work began and spent more than 40 years on it; he is buried in its crypt.

q: How tall is the Motherland Calls statue in Volgograd, Russia, to the tip of her sword?
hint: For scale: Rio’s Christ the Redeemer is about {30 m} tall.
clue: India’s Statue of Unity is about {182 m} tall.
card: When it was finished in 1967 it was the tallest statue in the world.

q: How tall is the Sky Tower in Auckland, New Zealand?
hint: For scale: Seattle’s Space Needle is about {184 m} tall.
clue: Berlin’s TV Tower stands {368 m} tall.
card: Visitors can jump off it on a guide cable from a ledge {192 m} up.

q: How long is the main span of Japan’s Akashi Kaikyō Bridge?
hint: For scale: the Golden Gate Bridge’s main span is about {1,280 m}.
clue: Denmark’s Great Belt Bridge has a main span of {1,624 m}.
card: An earthquake in 1995 moved its towers apart while it was being built, stretching the span by almost a meter.

q: In what year did China’s Chang’e 4 make the first landing on the far side of the Moon?
hint: For scale: the last Apollo astronauts left the Moon in 1972.
clue: Japan’s SLIM lander touched down on the Moon in 2024.
card: Because the far side never faces Earth, it talked to home through a relay satellite parked beyond the Moon.

q: Roughly how high does Olympus Mons, the giant volcano on Mars, rise above the planet’s average surface level?
hint: For scale: Mount Everest is about {8.8 km} above sea level.
clue: Hawaii’s Mauna Kea stands about {10 km} tall from its base on the seafloor.
card: It is so broad, about the size of Poland, that someone on its slopes couldn’t see the summit over the horizon.

q: In what year did SpaceX first land an orbital rocket’s booster back on the ground?
hint: For scale: SpaceX was founded in 2002.
clue: SpaceX first flew astronauts to the International Space Station in 2020.
card: The Falcon 9 booster touched down at Cape Canaveral about ten minutes after it launched.

q: How long is Valles Marineris, the giant canyon system on Mars?
hint: For scale: Mars is about {6,800 km} wide.
clue: The Danube river runs about {2,850 km}.
card: It is up to {7 km} deep, about four times the depth of the Grand Canyon.

q: How high above Earth do GPS satellites orbit?
hint: For scale: the International Space Station orbits about {400 km} up.
clue: Geostationary weather satellites sit about {35,786 km} up.
card: Their clocks run fast by about 38 microseconds a day because of relativity, and the system corrects for it.

q: How fast is Voyager 1 traveling away from the Sun?
hint: For scale: a rifle bullet flies at about {1 km/s}.
clue: Earth orbits the Sun at about {30 km/s}.
card: Launched in 1977, it is the most distant human-made object, and its radio signals take about a day to reach us.

q: Roughly how wide was the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs?
hint: For scale: the crater it left in Mexico is about {180 km} wide.
clue: Mars’s moon Phobos is about {22 km} across.
card: The buried crater, near Chicxulub on Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula, was only linked to the impact in 1991.

q: How deep is the deepest dive ever recorded for an emperor penguin?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower is about {330 m} tall.
clue: Tokyo Skytree is {634 m} tall.
card: On a hunting dive it can stay underwater for about 20 minutes on a single breath.

q: In what year did Gregor Mendel publish his pea-plant experiments, founding genetics?
hint: For scale: Mendel was born in 1822, in what is now the Czech Republic.
clue: Darwin published On the Origin of Species in 1859.
card: Hardly anyone noticed; his work was rediscovered in 1900, 16 years after his death.

q: How large is the Amazon rainforest?
hint: For scale: the United States covers about {9,800,000 sq km}.
clue: The European Union covers about {4,200,000 sq km}.
card: About 60% of it lies in Brazil, and it holds an estimated 390 billion trees.

q: How many living species of zebra are there?
hint: For scale: zebras belong to the horse family, alongside donkeys and wild asses.
clue: There are two living species of hippopotamus.
card: No two zebras have the same stripe pattern, much like human fingerprints.

q: In what year did Charles Darwin visit the Galápagos Islands aboard HMS Beagle?
hint: For scale: Napoleon was defeated at Waterloo in 1815.
clue: The first intercity passenger railway, Liverpool to Manchester, opened in 1830.
card: He stayed only about five weeks, but the islands’ finches and tortoises shaped his thinking for decades.

q: How many legs does Eumillipes persephone, the leggiest animal ever found, have?
hint: For scale: most millipedes have fewer than 400 legs.
clue: The previous record holder, a California millipede, had 750 legs.
card: It was found in 2020, living deep underground in a mining borehole in Western Australia.

q: How many legs does a tardigrade (water bear) have?
hint: For scale: insects have six legs.
clue: A lobster has ten legs.
card: These tiny animals can survive drying out, freezing and even the vacuum of space.

q: In what year did Brazil declare independence from Portugal?
hint: For scale: Portugal’s royal court fled Napoleon to Rio de Janeiro in 1808.
clue: Argentina declared independence in 1816.
card: Its first emperor, Pedro I, was the son of Portugal’s own king, who had left him in charge.

q: In what year was Nelson Mandela released from prison?
hint: For scale: he was jailed in 1962.
clue: South Africa hosted and won the Rugby World Cup in 1995.
card: He had spent 27 years in prison, 18 of them on Robben Island.

q: For how many years did China’s Ming dynasty rule?
hint: For scale: the Ming took power in 1368, after about a century of Mongol rule.
clue: England’s Tudor dynasty ruled for 118 years.
card: Its emperors built most of the Great Wall that tourists walk today, as well as Beijing’s Forbidden City.

q: In what year did Hernán Cortés reach Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital?
hint: For scale: Columbus first reached the Americas in 1492.
clue: Francisco Pizarro captured the Inca emperor Atahualpa in 1532.
card: Tenochtitlan, built on a lake, was one of the largest cities on Earth; Mexico City now stands on its site.

q: In what year was the Republic of Turkey proclaimed?
hint: For scale: the Ottomans took Constantinople in 1453.
clue: World War I ended in 1918.
card: Its capital became Ankara rather than Istanbul, and Mustafa Kemal Atatürk became its first president.

q: In what year did Ghana become independent?
hint: For scale: India became independent in 1947.
clue: Libya became independent in 1951.
card: Led by Kwame Nkrumah, it was the first sub-Saharan colony in Africa to win its independence.

q: How long is China’s Grand Canal, the world’s longest canal?
hint: For scale: Egypt’s Suez Canal is about {193 km} long.
clue: The Rhine river is about {1,230 km} long.
card: Its oldest parts were dug about 2,500 years ago, and barges still use it today.

q: How many original Volkswagen Beetles were built?
hint: For scale: about 5.4 million original Minis were built.
clue: Ford built about 15 million Model Ts.
card: The last one rolled off the line in Puebla, Mexico, in 2003.

q: What top speed did the Shanghai Maglev hit on its regular passenger runs when it opened?
hint: For scale: France’s TGV trains run at up to {320 km/h} in service.
clue: A Formula One car tops out at about {360 km/h}.
card: It covers the {30 km} to Pudong Airport in about seven and a half minutes.

q: In what year did Honda launch the Super Cub, the best-selling motor vehicle ever?
hint: For scale: Piaggio’s first Vespa went on sale in 1946.
clue: The first Toyota Corolla went on sale in 1966.
card: More than 100 million have been made, more than any other motor vehicle in history.

q: How heavy can a fully loaded Airbus A380 be at takeoff?
hint: For scale: a Boeing 747-400 can take off at up to about {397 t}.
clue: The Antonov An-225 could take off at {640 t}.
card: About half of that weight can be fuel, passengers and cargo.

q: How long is the ring of CERN’s Large Hadron Collider, under the France–Switzerland border?
hint: For scale: a marathon is about {42 km}.
clue: Paris’s Périphérique ring road runs about {35 km} around the city.
card: Its protons race around the ring more than 11,000 times a second, just under the speed of light.

q: In what year did Karl Drais first ride his “running machine,” the ancestor of the bicycle?
hint: For scale: the French Revolution began in 1789.
clue: The first public steam railway, Stockton to Darlington, opened in 1825.
card: It had no pedals: riders pushed along with their feet, like a child’s balance bike.

q: What speed did Ken Warby’s boat Spirit of Australia reach in 1978, setting the water speed record?
hint: For scale: Japan’s first bullet trains ran at {210 km/h}.
clue: Japan’s L0 maglev train has hit {603 km/h}.
card: Warby built the boat largely in his own backyard in Sydney.

q: How tall is Mont Blanc, the highest mountain in the Alps?
hint: For scale: Mount Everest is about {8,849 m} tall.
clue: Russia’s Mount Elbrus stands {5,642 m} tall.
card: Its height shifts a little from year to year as the ice cap on its summit grows and shrinks.

q: How wide is the Strait of Gibraltar at its narrowest?
hint: For scale: Istanbul’s Bosphorus is under {1 km} wide at its narrowest.
clue: The Strait of Dover between England and France is about {33 km} wide.
card: It is the only natural link between the Mediterranean and the Atlantic, with Spain on one side and Morocco on the other.

q: How many countries share a land border with Brazil?
hint: For scale: Russia shares land borders with 14 countries.
clue: Austria shares land borders with 8 countries.
card: One of them is France, through French Guiana, and it is France’s longest land border.

q: How large is the Caspian Sea, the world’s largest inland body of water?
hint: For scale: France covers about {550,000 sq km}.
clue: Italy covers about {301,000 sq km}.
card: Its water is about a third as salty as the ocean, and five countries share its shores.

q: How long is Earth’s equator?
hint: For scale: a flight from London to Sydney covers about {17,000 km}.
clue: The Great Wall of China, every branch counted, runs about {21,200 km}.
card: The meter was first defined so that the North Pole would be exactly ten million meters from the equator.

q: How many letters are in the Arabic alphabet?
hint: For scale: Japanese hiragana has 46 basic characters.
clue: The Hebrew alphabet has 22 letters.
card: Only consonants and long vowels get letters; short vowels are usually left unwritten.

q: How long is a €5 banknote?
hint: For scale: a credit card is about {86 mm} long.
clue: The largest euro note, the €500, is {160 mm} long.
card: Each euro note is longer than the one below it in value, so people with poor eyesight can tell them apart.
